test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which authority introduced updated rules for biological resource regulation in India in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Biodiversity Authority**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)** is the primary regulatory body in India responsible for the implementation of the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**.
 
• In **2025**, the authority introduced updated rules and guidelines to streamline the process of accessing **biological resources** and associated knowledge, focusing on **Ease of Doing Business** while maintaining conservation standards.
 
• The **NBA** is a statutory autonomous body established in **2003** under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**, with its headquarters located in **Chennai**.
 
• The updated **2025** regulations further refine the **Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS)** mechanism, ensuring that the benefits derived from the commercial use of biological resources are shared equitably with local **Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)**.
 
• The authority performs a facilitative and advisory role to the **Government of India** on issues related to the conservation of biodiversity and the sustainable use of its components. ***Hence, the correct answer is National Biodiversity Authority.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Biological Diversity Act, 2002:**
 
 
• This Act was enacted to meet the obligations under the **United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)**, to which India became a party in **1994**.
 
• It aims at the **conservation** of biological resources, their **sustainable use**, and the **fair and equitable sharing** of benefits arising out of the use of biological resources.
 
 
 
• **Institutional Structure:**
 
 
• The Act provides for a **three-tier institutional structure**: the **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)** at the national level, **State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs)** at the state level, and **Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs)** at the local level (Panchayats and Municipalities).
 
• The **BMCs** are responsible for preparing **People’s Biodiversity Registers (PBRs)**, which document local biological resources and traditional knowledge.
 
 
 
• **Recent Legislative Changes:**
 
 
• The **Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023**, laid the groundwork for the **2025 rules** by decriminalizing certain offenses and exempting **AYUSH practitioners** and cultivated medicinal plants from certain compliance requirements.
 
• The **2023 amendment** also sought to encourage **foreign investment** in the sector while safeguarding the interests of **indigenous communities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Scope:** The **NBA** regulates activities such as the commercial utilization of biological resources, **bio-survey**, and **bio-utilization** by non-Indians or foreign entities.
 
• **Intellectual Property Rights (IPR):** Any person or entity seeking **Intellectual Property Rights** for an invention based on biological resources or knowledge obtained from **India** must obtain prior approval from the **NBA**.
 
• **Global Context:** The **NBA** also works to ensure compliance with the **Nagoya Protocol** on Access and Benefit Sharing, which was adopted in **2010** and came into force in **2014**.
 
• **Conservation Sites:** The **National Biodiversity Authority** has the power to notify areas of biodiversity importance as **Biodiversity Heritage Sites (BHS)** in consultation with local bodies.
